mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate increases by more than 0.25% over the next month, higher discount rates reduce the present value of expected corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the following 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or near-zero during the trigger, or FEDFUNDS increase is < 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in PAYEMS (labor market additions) above 10,000 monthly coincides with increased hiring optimism, which elevates expected corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: No significant return correlation over 60 days after the trigger, or earnings revisions remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: When HOUST (industrial production) unexpectedly exceeds prior month by 2% and CPIAUCSL (inflation) is below 0.5%, it signals a resilient demand environment that supports positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or statistically insignificant, or inflation spikes above 0.5% during the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of 3% over two months indicates supply-side weakness, which reduces market confidence and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive or near-zero, or INDPRO recovers >3% in the next month.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent FEDFUNDS below 4%, the lower discount rate increases the present value of equities, resulting in positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns regardless of other signals.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative, or FEDFUNDS rise above 4% during the window.

mechanism_narrative: UNRATE falling below 4% for three consecutive months suggests labor market slackening, which reduces earnings growth expectations and drives negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Forward returns are positive or unchanged, or UNRATE recovers above 4% within the window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in RSAFS (available for sale securities) above 200,000 in a month indicates financial market stress, which elevates risk premia and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: Forward returns are positive or not significantly different from baseline, or RSAFS decline instead.

mechanism_narrative: When both INDPRO and GDPC1 show simultaneous contraction of 2% over the next quarter, it reflects dual supply and demand pressures that depress market valuations and drive negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous_3mo average * 0.98 AND GDPC1 < previous_3mo average * 0.98
regime_hint: Dual contraction in output and orders
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or statistically insignificant, or either series recovers >2% in the window.
